summary: Norman Mosley Penzer was an Indologist who earned an M.A. from the University of Cambridge (~1910–1913). In 1925, he held memberships and fellowships in the Folklore Society, Royal Anthropological Institute, Royal Asiatic Society, Royal Geographical Society, and Geological Society.

Norvin J. Hein was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Franklin Edgerton. He served as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion in the Divinity School at Yale University (attested 1965).

Nosei Fuji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University. He taught at Daegu University, directed institutes at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College and the Buddhist Cultural Institute, and served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at Ryukoku University (2011–2013).

Notto R. Thelle is a scholar of religious, Buddhist, and Japanese studies. He studied at the University of Oslo and the Norwegian Academy of Music, held posts at the NCC Center (1974) and Oslo Metropolitan University, and served at the University of Oslo (~1986–2006).

Noémie Verdon works in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne (up to 2015) under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and later held a post at Kyoto University (attested 2018–2019).

Noël Peri was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and sinology who studied at the Séminaire de Saint-Sulpice (~1883–1888). He served the Paris Foreign Missions Society, taught music at Tokyo University of the Arts, and worked at the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Nyanaponika Thera was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nyanatiloka Mahathera, Anton Walter Florus Gueth, and Mahasi Sayadaw, and attended the University of Peradeniya. He headed the Forest Hermitage (1952) and co-founded and led the Buddhist Publication Society (1958–1988).

Nyingcha Duoji is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Boston University and completed his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp and teacher Mark Elliott.

Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen studied under Patrul Rinpoche (~1855–1880), Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He studied at Katok and Nyoshul Monasteries and under Dudjom Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, later teaching numerous disciples.
Nyoten Jinbo was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami and served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Odette Viennot was an Indology and art history scholar who studied at École du Louvre and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Philippe Stern. She worked at the Guimet Museum (1951) and the National Centre for Scientific Research (~1954–1976).
Odolen Smékal was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Vincenc Pořízka and earned his Ph.D. from Charles University in 1952. He began teaching Hindi at Charles University in 1954.
Ofer Peres is an Indology and religious studies scholar who has held posts at the South Asia Institute at Heidelberg University and at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 2026).

Ogyen Trinley Dorje is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, Bokar Rinpoche, Pema Donyo Nyinje, Drub Pön Dechen Rinpoche, and Dragpa Tenpa Yarpel, and taught Khenpo Sherab Püntsok.
Ohryu Matsushima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and held a post there.

Oktiabrina Volkova was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1947–1952) and under Bidia Dandaron. She taught at the Moscow State Institute of International Relations and was a researcher at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies.

Olaf Hansen was an Iranian and Central Asian studies linguist. He studied at the University of Hamburg under Hans Reichelt, held posts at Berlin State Museums, Humboldt, Jena, and the GDR Academy of Sciences, and served as Professor at Free University of Berlin (1950–1968).

Olav Hackstein is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at Pennsylvania, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and EPHE, becoming a full professor at the University of Munich in 2008.

Oldřich Friš was a Czech Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University (PhD ~1921–1946) under Vincenc Lesný and others. He served as acting professor at Palacký University Olomouc and later held posts as assistant professor and section director at Charles University.
